ASSISTANT:
It's difficult to pinpoint one single jazz musician as the most influential in the 1950s, as there were many important figures who contributed to the development of the genre during that time. However, some of the most significant and influential musicians of the era include Miles Davis, John Coltrane, and Thelonious Monk, who helped pioneer the bebop and post-bop styles of jazz. Other notable figures such as Duke Ellington, Charlie Parker, and Dizzy Gillespie also continued to make important contributions to the genre during this decade.
